challenges.heading: What makes enterprise UX harder than consumer UX?
challenges.rule: 6 cards. Title 3–6 words; body 30–55 words with one sourced fact or one concrete example. US frame. No hedges.

cards.title: One product, many roles
points: the buyer (IT, procurement, security) is not the daily user
admins, managers, operators, approvers and guests see different modules and actions
define role-based access control (RBAC) with the NIST CSRC definition: access authorizations attached to roles, not to individuals

cards.title: Screens full of data
points: tables with dozens of columns, filters, sorting, inline edits and bulk actions
IBM Carbon's data table guidance: sortable headers, expandable rows, batch actions, and the table is not a spreadsheet replacement
Salesforce lightning-datatable is not supported on mobile, so plan desktop-first

cards.title: Security reviews before purchase
points: enterprise buyers send security questionnaires and ask for a SOC 2 report
SOC 2 is an attestation by an independent CPA firm against the AICPA Trust Services Criteria: security (required), availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy
the interface has to show the controls: SSO, MFA enforcement, audit logs, role changes

cards.title: Accessibility in the contract
points: federal buyers procure under the Revised Section 508 Standards (final rule January 18, 2017; compliance from January 18, 2018), which incorporate WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA
vendors document conformance in an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) built on the VPAT
state and local government buyers fall under the ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA)

cards.title: AI features staff do not trust
points: 37% of US firms with at least 250 employees reported using AI (Census Bureau, December 2025–May 2026)
a wrong answer in a finance or HR workflow costs more than in a consumer app
staff need sources, review and an undo before they rely on output

cards.title: Adoption after rollout
points: power users lose habits, shortcuts and saved views when an interface changes
employees already work across many apps: 101 apps per company is Okta's 2024 global average
a launch without a rollout plan fills the help desk queue

faqs.heading: Enterprise UX FAQs from product, IT and security leads
faqs.rule: 6 FAQs. Boolean questions start with Yes or No. Answers 40–80 words, open (not collapsed), one link at most each.

items.answerHint: Definition with the keyword as subject: UX design of software organizations buy and deploy for employees and partners (SaaS platforms, internal tools, ERP and CRM-type systems). It differs from consumer UX through many roles, buyer ≠ user, dense data and long daily sessions, and it is judged by task time and errors rather than delight.

items.q: How is enterprise UX design different for AI features?
items.answerHint: AI output changes and can be wrong, so enterprise UX adds sources, human review, approval steps and an activity log. NIST AI RMF 1.0 (January 26, 2023, voluntary) and the Generative AI Profile NIST-AI-600-1 (July 26, 2024) give the risk vocabulary. Link /services/ai-products/ai-ux-design-agency/.

items.q: Can you design enterprise software for Section 508 and WCAG 2.2 AA?
items.answerHint: Yes. WCAG 2.2 became a W3C Recommendation on October 5, 2023 and adds 9 success criteria over 2.1; content that meets 2.2 also meets 2.1 and 2.0. Section 508 legally references WCAG 2.0 A/AA, so designing to 2.2 AA covers it. We annotate designs; the ACR is completed by your team or an accessibility auditor. Do NOT say we issue VPATs or certify conformance.

items.q: Do you help enterprise products pass SOC 2 security reviews?
items.answerHint: Yes, on the interface side only. SOC 2 is an attestation by an independent CPA firm against the AICPA Trust Services Criteria; security is required in every report. We design the screens reviewers ask to see: SSO and MFA settings, SCIM provisioning, role changes, audit logs and access reviews. We do not audit or certify. Do not claim ui-ux.agency or tkxel holds a SOC 2 report.

items.q: How do you get employees to adopt a redesigned enterprise tool?
items.answerHint: Ship in phases behind feature flags, start with a beta group, keep an optional switch back during the beta, use in-app announcements and a short tour, and measure task time and support tickets before and after. Deep link /services/saas-products/saas-product-redesign/#how-does-our-saas-product-redesign-avoid-a-big-bang-launch.

items.q: How much does enterprise UX design cost?
items.answerHint: Only published ranges: full SaaS product $40,000–$180,000; phased redesign $50,000–$200,000 over 8–20 weeks; AI UX design $25,000–$90,000; embedded team $15,000–$40,000 per month. Number of roles, workflows and platforms set the price. Link /services/ui-ux-design-cost/. No new enterprise-only price.

eav.value: Enterprise UX is the user experience design of software that organizations buy and deploy for employees and partners, such as SaaS platforms, internal tools, ERP and CRM systems.
One enterprise product serves admins, operators, managers and buyers inside the same product.
B2B platforms with complex roles and data tables; copilots, AI agents and internal AI tools for operations teams.
4 steps over 6 to 16 weeks: review (1–2 weeks), flows and wireframes (2–4), UI and design system (2–6), build support (1–4).
$40,000–$180,000 for a full SaaS product; $50,000–$200,000 for a phased redesign; $25,000–$90,000 for AI UX design; $15,000–$40,000 per month for an embedded team.
Mass Media Co. B2B platform: order processing efficiency +30%, order processing error rate 2+ (reduced from 25%), task completion +3%.
Access authorizations are attached to roles, and a user gets them by being assigned the role.
SCIM (IETF RFC 7644, Proposed Standard, September 2015) is an HTTP protocol for managing identities in enterprise-to-cloud and inter-cloud scenarios.

An independent CPA firm attests to a service organization's controls against 5 Trust Services Criteria: security (required), availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. Type 1 covers design at a point in time; Type 2 covers operating effectiveness over a period.
Revised 508 Standards: final rule January 18, 2017, compliance from January 18, 2018; incorporate WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA by reference for web, documents and software procured by federal agencies.
Federal contract language requires ICT delivered under a work statement to conform to the Revised 508 Standards.
Vendors document conformance in an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) built on the VPAT template.
W3C Recommendation on October 5, 2023; adds 9 success criteria over WCAG 2.1; SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) requires 24 × 24 CSS pixels at Level AA.

The 2024 DOJ rule requires state and local government web content and mobile apps to meet WCAG 2.1 AA; an April 20, 2026 interim final rule moved compliance to April 26, 2027 (50,000+ population) and April 26, 2028 (smaller entities).
